# DOSXYZ source-21 smoke fixtures

These inputs exercise BEAM shared-library sampling, the configured native
particleDmlc source bridge, and the ordinary DOSXYZ transport call. They are
synthetic wiring fixtures, not commissioned machine data or dose references.

- `EXslabs_mcdose_source21.egsinp` emits 1 MeV photons through the stock SLABS
  shape and rejects BEAM products below 100 keV.
- `dosxyznrc_mcdose_source21.egsinp` selects source 21 with the
  `mcdose_particle_dmlc` token, two fractional-MU settings, one requested
  history, and one-way photon splitting. Its synthetic surrounding-air region
  extends 110 cm from the phantom so that the 100 cm source plane is inside
  the DOSXYZ geometry; source 21 transports from that plane rather than first
  projecting particles to the phantom boundary.

The startup artifact must be generated by the monte-carlo repository's
`tests/acceptance/write_particle_dmlc_source21_smoke_startup.py`. Its synthetic
aperture and section rows cover the fixture's complete BEAM field, so valid
products exercise the zero-equivalent-thickness pass path. Its attenuation
table starts at the 10 keV DOSXYZ transport cutoff as a defensive bound. Those
test-only values must not be substituted for a commissioned machine profile.

The DOSXYZ patch is pinned to EGSnrc commit
`9edee3ebfda3d81d0e8eb033a7e76bf9a70e41ef`. Apply it with zero fuzz in an
isolated user-code copy; do not patch an active clinical or stock EGSnrc tree.
Its source-2 patient-frame mode is opt-in and intended for post-delivery IAEA
phase spaces whose coordinates have already been transformed toward the
patient. Unflagged source 2 retains the upstream source-plane semantics.
